title: The Importance of Unemployment Risk for Individual Savings
package_mismatch_note: readme.rtf uses the working title 'The Savings and Employment Effects of Higher Job Loss Risk' (same authors, same oil-shock design); treated as the same paper.
eligible_reason: Single-date DiD, not staggered. The treatment is the 2014 oil-price collapse: run_all.do line 136-137 sets post = 1 if year > 2013 for every individual, and the main Tables 2-5 interact post with engin13 (engineers vs academics/government high-skilled in oil regions, 2013 occupation), reghdfe bankinnsk post##engin13 ..., absorb(id year) cluster(id). All treated individuals share one first-treated year (2014); Table 6 uses post = year > 2014 on collapsed group means (again one date); Table 3 adds a tenure triple interaction. One adoption cohort only. In addition, the package ships only a synthetic dataset.
design_notes: Stata 17, reghdfe and xtreg fe; all code in run_all.do. Individual-year panel 2010-2014 or 2010-2016, sample restricted to engineers and academic/government high-skilled in oil regions not unemployed in 2014-15 (or 2014-16). Outcomes: bank deposits (bankinnsk), risky financial assets, illiquid assets. The abstract's 1.3% per percentage point of unemployment is a scaling of the reduced-form DiD by the change in unemployment rates.
data_files_note: readme.rtf: Statistics Norway register data must be requested from SSB; 'the authors include a synthetic dataset ... [that] mimics the setup of the actual data'. data.dta: 23,000 rows, exactly 1,000 ids per year 2000-2022.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). Single common treatment date (2014 oil shock) and synthetic data; excluded on both grounds.
